claims.text: Akron ranks 33rd of 56 polymer metros on nominal wages and 19th on price-adjusted wages, a climb of 14 places; the comparison set is the 56 metros with at least 2,000 polymer jobs (standfirst, hero cards, slope figure title and annotation, mobile rank list). Extended 2026-08-27 from the rank-only assertion: the climb, the set size and the floor are now asserted too, because all three are hand-typed on the page.
claims.source: BLS QCEW 2023 NAICS 326 metro weekly wage; BEA MARPP 2023 all-items price parity
claims.assert: (lambda a: a['big_rank_nominal'] == 33 and a['big_rank_real'] == 19 and a['big_climb'] == 14)([r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0]) and len(D['big']) == 56 and D['meta']['n_big'] == 56 and D['meta']['big_floor'] == 2000
claims.actual: [(r['big_rank_nominal'], r['big_rank_real'], r['big_climb'], len(D['big']), D['meta']['big_floor']) for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420']
claims.falsified_if: Either source revises, or the 2,000-job floor changes. The floor is a CHOICE — it selects the comparison set, and a different floor gives a different rank. State the floor whenever the rank is quoted.

claims.text: The adjustment moves Akron from below the median polymer metro to above it.
claims.source: derived: median nominal and median real across the 56-metro set
claims.assert: (lambda B, a: a['nominal'] < sorted(r['nominal'] for r in B)[len(B)//2] and a['real'] > sorted(r['real'] for r in B)[len(B)//2])(D['big'], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.actual: (sorted(r['nominal'] for r in D['big'])[len(D['big'])//2], sorted(r['real'] for r in D['big'])[len(D['big'])//2], [(r['nominal'], r['real']) for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'])
claims.falsified_if: Akron's wage rises or falls past the median in either measure. Crossing the median is the entire claim; if it stops crossing, the page has no finding and should say so.

claims.text: Akron is a median-price metro, not a cheap one: more than a hundred metros are cheaper.
claims.source: BEA MARPP 2023, all items, 235 metros with a disclosed polymer wage
claims.assert: len([r for r in D['metros'] if r['rpp'] < [x for x in D['metros'] if x['area']=='10420'][0]['rpp']]) > 100
claims.actual: (len([r for r in D['metros'] if r['rpp'] < [x for x in D['metros'] if x['area']=='10420'][0]['rpp']]), len(D['metros']))
claims.falsified_if: Akron's price level falls relative to other metros. This claim exists to stop the page being read as a 'low cost of living' pitch — the advantage is relative to where the polymer industry sits, not to the country.

claims.text: The strip figure subtitle hand-types three values: 235 metros, Akron at 92.9, the median metro at 93.1 (strip fig-sub; svg title).
claims.source: BEA MARPP 2023 all items; median convention matches the page's JS (sorted, floor(n/2))
claims.assert: len(D['metros']) == 235 and D['meta']['n_metros'] == 235 and abs([r for r in D['metros'] if r['area']=='10420'][0]['rpp'] - 92.9) <= 0.05 and abs(sorted(r['rpp'] for r in D['metros'])[len(D['metros'])//2] - 93.1) <= 0.05
claims.actual: (len(D['metros']), [r['rpp'] for r in D['metros'] if r['area']=='10420'], sorted(r['rpp'] for r in D['metros'])[len(D['metros'])//2])
claims.falsified_if: A revision moves Akron's price level or the median off the one-decimal values typed in the subtitle, or the disclosed-metro count leaves 235.

claims.text: The same paycheck stretches about 10 percent further in Akron than in Chicago (standfirst).
claims.source: derived: Chicago RPP over Akron RPP, minus one
claims.assert: (lambda c, a: 0.095 <= c['rpp']/a['rpp'] - 1 <= 0.11)([r for r in D['big'] if 'Chicago' in r['name']][0], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.actual: (lambda c, a: c['rpp']/a['rpp'] - 1)([r for r in D['big'] if 'Chicago' in r['name']][0], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.falsified_if: Either metro's price parity revises enough that the ratio leaves 9.5-11 percent, so 'about 10 percent' no longer rounds from the data.

claims.text: The three steepest falls in the 56-metro ranking are San Francisco, Seattle and New York, falling 24 to 29 places (slope bracket annotation, svg title, lede's 'steepest falls' framing).
claims.source: derived: big_climb sorted ascending, first three
claims.assert: (lambda f: all(any(n in r['name'] for r in f) for n in ('San Francisco', 'Seattle', 'New York')) and min(-r['big_climb'] for r in f) == 24 and max(-r['big_climb'] for r in f) == 29)(sorted(D['big'], key=lambda r: r['big_climb'])[:3])
claims.actual: [(r['name'], r['big_climb']) for r in sorted(D['big'], key=lambda r: r['big_climb'])[:3]]
claims.falsified_if: A revision reorders the biggest fallers or moves the fall magnitudes off the 24-29 range typed in the bracket.

claims.text: The industry's biggest employers sit where the same salary buys up to a fifth less than in Akron (scatter figure title; dropped from the closer 2026-08-28 to bring the closer under its 90-word budget). 'Biggest employers' means the five largest big-metro polymer employers; the maximum shortfall among them is Los Angeles at about 19 percent. Corrected 2026-08-27: the previous closer said 'a quarter less', which no metro on the page reaches (the maximum anywhere in the set is San Francisco at 21 percent).
claims.source: derived: 1 - Akron RPP / metro RPP over the five largest employers
claims.assert: (lambda t5, a: 0.165 <= max(1 - a['rpp']/r['rpp'] for r in t5) <= 0.215)(sorted(D['big'], key=lambda r: -r['emp'])[:5], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.actual: (lambda t5, a: [(r['name'], round(1 - a['rpp']/r['rpp'], 3)) for r in t5])(sorted(D['big'], key=lambda r: -r['emp'])[:5], [r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.falsified_if: Price parities revise so the largest shortfall among the top-five employers leaves 16.5-21.5 percent, and 'a fifth' stops being the honest round.

claims.text: 14 of the 56 metros pay more on paper than Akron and buy less, New York, Los Angeles and Seattle among them (default verdict sentence, and the closer's qualifying paragraph, where the three named metros moved 2026-08-28 out of the display statement).
claims.source: derived: nominal above Akron's and real below Akron's
claims.assert: (lambda F: len(F) == 14 and all(any(n in r['name'] for r in F) for n in ('New York', 'Los Angeles', 'Seattle')))((lambda a: [r for r in D['big'] if r['nominal'] > a['nominal'] and r['real'] < a['real']])([r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0]))
claims.actual: (lambda a: [(r['name'], r['nominal'], round(r['real'], 1)) for r in D['big'] if r['nominal'] > a['nominal'] and r['real'] < a['real']])([r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0])
claims.falsified_if: A revision changes the count of outright flips or drops any of the three named metros out of the set. The named metros are the ones a recruiter actually loses candidates to; if one leaves, the closer must be rewritten.

claims.text: Akron's average polymer paycheck is $1,238 a week (about $64,000 a year) and buys like $1,332; matching its buying power takes about $71,000 in Chicago (a wedge of about $6,600) and about $81,000 in San Francisco (human-scale band, closer, comparator default and template).
claims.source: derived: Akron nominal scaled by each rival's RPP ratio, annualized at 52 weeks
claims.assert: (lambda a, c, s: a['nominal'] == 1238 and abs(a['real'] - 1332.3) <= 0.5 and abs(a['nominal']*52 - 64000) <= 600 and abs(a['nominal']*c['rpp']/a['rpp']*52 - 71000) <= 600 and abs((a['nominal']*c['rpp']/a['rpp'] - a['nominal'])*52 - 6600) <= 300 and abs(a['nominal']*s['rpp']/a['rpp']*52 - 81000) <= 800)([r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0], [r for r in D['big'] if 'Chicago' in r['name']][0], [r for r in D['big'] if 'San Francisco' in r['name']][0])
claims.actual: (lambda a, c, s: (a['nominal'], a['real'], round(a['nominal']*52), round(a['nominal']*c['rpp']/a['rpp']*52), round((a['nominal']*c['rpp']/a['rpp'] - a['nominal'])*52), round(a['nominal']*s['rpp']/a['rpp']*52)))([r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'][0], [r for r in D['big'] if 'Chicago' in r['name']][0], [r for r in D['big'] if 'San Francisco' in r['name']][0])
claims.falsified_if: Any of the annualized figures stops rounding to the hand-typed $64,000 / $71,000 / $6,600 / $81,000. Per-rival sentences composed by the picker are variants of this same arithmetic and are covered by it plus rw-flip; only the default state is asserted directly.

claims.text: Everything on this page is the 2023 release; no earlier year ships with it, so the 14-place climb is shown without a track record (slope source line, and since 2026-08-28 the drawn '2023 only, one print' cue under the +14 annotation on both the desktop slope and the mobile rank list). This sentence must be replaced by a persistence test the moment prior-year pairs are added to the data.
claims.source: data file inventory: meta.year and the absence of any multi-year series
claims.assert: D['meta']['year'] == 2023 and 'trend' not in D and sorted(D.keys()) == ['big', 'home', 'meta', 'metros']
claims.falsified_if: A rebuilt data file carries 2021/2022 pairs (or any 'trend' key). Then the honest move inverts: drop this disclaimer and show whether the climb repeats across releases.

claims.text: This page is metro-level throughout and never uses the PIC-12 county footprint; the region appears through the Akron metro area alone, because Cleveland and Canton have no disclosed 2023 polymer wage (band 1 gloss, slope source line, slope table note, methodology). Rewritten 2026-08-28: the pre-hero footprint banner that used to carry this was removed, so the sentence is now asserted where a reader actually meets it.
claims.source: BEA publishes price parities only for metros; they cannot be summed to counties. Absence of Cleveland and Canton is read off the shipped metro set, not asserted from memory.
claims.assert: 'Metro, not county' in D['meta']['geography'] and all(len(r['area']) == 5 for r in D['metros']) and len([r for r in D['metros'] if 'Cleveland' in r['name'] or 'Canton' in r['name']]) == 0 and len([r for r in D['metros'] if r['area'] == '10420']) == 1
claims.actual: (D['meta']['geography'], [r['name'] for r in D['metros'] if 'Cleveland' in r['name'] or 'Canton' in r['name']])
claims.falsified_if: Anyone joins this to county QCEW or to the vault, or a later QCEW release discloses Cleveland or Canton. If either metro appears in the data, 'the region appears through Akron alone' is false on the page and in the byline scope, and both must be rewritten before the next publish.

claims.text: Both figure source lines and the byline name the same two sources and year: BLS QCEW and BEA Regional Price Parities, 2023 (slope source line, scatter source line, hero byline). Added 2026-08-28 because those strings are now hand-typed in the page rather than interpolated from meta.source, which the caveat-ink budget could not carry.
claims.source: data file meta.source, which the derive script writes from the fetch parameters
claims.assert: 'QCEW' in D['meta']['source'] and 'Regional Price Parities' in D['meta']['source'] and str(D['meta']['year']) in D['meta']['source'] and D['meta']['year'] == 2023
claims.falsified_if: The page is rebuilt on a different vintage or a different price index, so the hand-typed attribution stops matching meta.source. Any year change must be made in three visible places, not one.
